title: Day 15 of making an RTS game for agents: Neon is beating old Astra
author: asimpleabstraction
selftext:
Hey all! Had great comments in a prev post wanted to share here

I've been running agents against my benchmarking CLI that kicks off FULL gameplay matches against a frozen set of bot policies... each having a different difficulty tier (ala StarSkirmish)

To my surprise, GPT-6.2 Sol is kicking butt against almost all models. In the simulation, agents have to do a BUNCH of highly complex reasoning and decision making, like:

1. Manage four planes of DIFFEREING strategic play style (complex policy writing)
2. Manage a global pool of shared resources (scarcity)
3. Decide on queueing units across multiple planes (attention)
4. Defend, attack, micro, and write bot policies all at once
5. Possibly work together with different agents that are different models (behavior diversity)
6. Possibly work with a human (play well with a completely different cognitive architecture)

Going to continue to throw bots at this.. any models I should run this against?

What's unique IMO is the world complexity... matches are symmetric so we can bet on the invariance of each bot behavior per version, so that part it (I think) rigorous.

Would love thoughts and feedback!
